Ridiculous ads. 2.5 stars. I’ve used this app for tracking my period for a couple years, and it was great, easily 4-5 stars. But now the ads on an app supposed to be designed to help navigate period health is just insane. As soon as I open the app I’m immediately bombarded by a pop up ad. Then when I go to log my period, a 30 second, irrelevant and unskippable ad pops up immediately. Seriously? I’m so sick of literally everything having ads these days, and companies doing anything to fill their pockets more. Having ads on an app for tracking a period is just ridiculous. The actual logging part is pretty detailed, and you can log other symptoms such as headache and nausea in addition to cramping and flow, which is what drew me to the app in the first place. But I’m really frustrated with these new ads and it really lowered the experience for me.

Edit: There also used to be very sexual articles that you were forced to see on the homepage with no way to toggle on or off in one of the updates, which was extremely annoying to someone who had no desire to see that. But since then it seems they have removed that “feature”, which is why I added another .5 stars. Having that feature before was quite obscene, because the purpose of the app is to track periods/pregnancy and not a blog for learning more sex positions or pleasures, especially with the large user interface of young girls starting their period who don’t need to be exposed to that, so I’m glad they seem to have removed it.

Meh. This period tracking app has several drawbacks, making it difficult to use. The accuracy of the app is questionable, and the numerous ads that pop up frequently make it frustrating to log your period. Even if you manage to overlook the ads, the app lacks notifications that could help you keep track of your menstrual cycle. On the positive side, the interface has a cute design, but it can be confusing to navigate. However, the app has inappropriate content related to sex that is not suitable for young children, especially girls under twelve years old. It's not a good idea to introduce such topics to young kids who might not understand their meaning just yet.
